bug_semantics: Winter CMS CombineAssets registers Storm's JavascriptImporter on .js assets. That filter inlines files named by =include/=require directives found in JS comment blocks. The target was concatenated to the including file's directory and resolved with realpath() with no root confinement and with no restriction that the target be a .js file (extension-less names had .js appended; named extensions such as .env were accepted). An authenticated cms.manage_assets user could therefore write a theme JS asset containing =include ../../../.env; the combiner inlined any PHP-readable file into the public combine/{file} response, which is served with no authn/authz, disclosing APP_KEY and database credentials to unauthenticated visitors. This is CWE-22 LFI through the JS importer, the JS counterpart of the earlier LESS @import issues, not a withdrawn advisory (CVE.org state PUBLISHED).
flaw_origin: The unconfined include sink was first written in wintercms/storm 0c6d68a554177de909247c255560d77b86748670 (2013-12-28, 'Add Assetic filters (Combiner)') as October\Rain\Combiner\Filter\JavaScript_Importer::directiveInclude: File::extension fallback to .js, then $scriptPath = realpath($this->scriptPath . '/' . $script) and File::get() with no PathResolver/withinAny/allowed-roots check. Subsequent Storm history only moves/renames/refactors that same realpath include (Support/Filters, Parse/Assetic, Assetic v3). Winter never owned the importer source; it only constructed new JavascriptImporter() from the 2014 October initial tree through e3300ce2. The 2026 Storm/Winter pair adds the missing .js-only and allowed-roots gates; those commits are remediations, not first-writes. AI trailers on the 2026 fixes are fix-only and do not attribute the 2013 BIC.
